daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The Constitutional Court ordered the government to explain reasons before blocking electronic information access, in a ruling that also mandated colour labels on food and beverage packaging containing sugar, salt, and other additives. The Constitutional Court continued hearings on Vice President Gibran's educational qualifications on 30 September, entering the evidentiary phase.

  • The Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK) alleged that Silmy Karim routinely gave money to Brawijaya University lecturers during doctoral supervision, with the KPK also investigating payments from both Silmy Karim and Bagus to prospective doctoral promotors.
  • Six suspects in the MBG governance corruption case will soon be brought to trial, with an active TNI officer named as a suspect alongside Dadan Hindayana and others.
  • Ombudsman uncovered serious irregularities at Cibinong Prison, including weekly extortion and a luxury house where corruptor Jimmy Masrin was seen.
  • A DPR member requested that the planned forensic audit of hajj finances not disrupt services for pilgrims, while BPKH stated it is ready to open its data for the audit.
  • Evidence in the hajj quota corruption trial revealed the trail of US$1 million and the relationship between former Religious Affairs Minister Yaqut and Nusron Wahid.
  • President Prabowo discussed narcotics eradication, highlighting prison overcapacity and rehabilitation issues during the briefing.
  • The Ministry of Religious Affairs proposed establishing technical staff for umrah supervision in the Holy Land to improve oversight of pilgrims.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia and Mongolia strengthened their partnership while commemorating 70 years of diplomatic relations, with the Indonesian Embassy facilitating business meetings between entrepreneurs from both countries and Mongolia expressing interest in expanding cooperation in pharmaceuticals and energy. Indonesian businesses offered coffee and seaweed products to the Mongolian market during the commemorative events.

  • The Indonesian military identified an OPM figure killed in a clash in Intan Jaya, Papua.
  • Indonesia stated it is ready to partner with Cambodia to eradicate online scams, with officials proposing strengthened cross-border coordination mechanisms to tackle online fraud.
  • The National Commission on Human Rights appreciated the Philippine president's pardon of Indonesian national Mary Jane Veloso.

Other

Indonesia held Pertalite fuel prices steady despite global oil prices surging to $107 per barrel, maintaining subsidized fuel affordability for consumers. The government is designing a prudent 2027 State Budget amid global economic risks, balancing fiscal sustainability with development needs.

  • Indonesia offered carbon market incentives to attract global green investors to participate in the country's climate finance initiatives.
  • The government allocated US$66.67 million to develop a modern fishery hub at Pengambengan port in Bali, aiming to create a world-class facility.
  • Danantara pledged to complete the LRT City project while emphasizing consumer protection and legal certainty for buyers.
  • State port operator Pelindo is cutting 17 subsidiaries to strengthen its business model and improve operational efficiency.
  • The glacier at Puncak Jaya in Papua is predicted to disappear completely by 2027, marking the end of Indonesia's only permanent snow cover.
  • Jakarta Governor Pramono said the capital remains safe despite influenza cases rising 15 percent in several regions across Indonesia.
